study_identification_part.si4_title: Revealing Individual Neuroanatomical Heterogeneity in Alzheimer Disease Using Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states objectives: to use neuroanatomical normative modeling of cortical thickness to characterize individual differences and outliers across AD, MCI, and controls; to assess relationships between cortical thickness heterogeneity and cognition, CSF biomarkers (Aβ, p-tau), and ApoE genotype; and to test whether heterogeneity predicts conversion from MCI to AD. These satisfy both criteria: hypotheses/questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: “we used neuroanatomical normative modeling to index regional patterns of variability in cortical thickness. We aimed to characterize individual differences and outliers in cortical thickness in patients with AD, people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and controls. Furthermore, we assessed the relationships between cortical thickness heterogeneity and cognitive function, β-amyloid, phosphorylated-tau, and ApoE genotype. Finally, we examined whether cortical thickness heterogeneity was predictive of conversion from MCI to AD.”

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study builds a new normative model using a large healthy reference dataset. It describes eligibility as healthy individuals across the lifespan from multiple public sources, specifies image quality control (Euler number filtering for the reference set), and reports the final reference sample size (n=33,072). However, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria and explicit reasons/counts for exclusions within the reference cohort are not fully enumerated in the main text (many specifics deferred to an external table/sources).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
“Participants were derived from 2 data sets: (1) a reference data set that comprised healthy people across the human lifespan... The reference data set was made by combining data on healthy people from multiple publicly available sources, including OASIS, ... and UKB...”
“Quality control of FreeSurfer processing for the reference data set relied on automated filtering median-centered absolute Euler number higher than 25...”
“In the reference data set, a total of n = 33,072 T1-weighted MRI scans were collated across 60 sites...”
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Verdi2023.pdf.md: Methods - Participants; Methods - Estimation of Cortical Thickness; Results - Participants

“...adaptively pools parameter estimates across sites via a shared prior... This simultaneously accounts for intersite variation...”

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The paper does not report an internal validation scheme (e.g., held-out test set, K-fold/LOOCV) for the reference normative model. The described partitioning pertains to transfer learning (70% of ADNI controls per site for recalibration) rather than model validation on unseen healthy reference data.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “...The parameters of the reference normative model were recalibrated to the ADNI data set using 70% of healthy controls per ADNI site... The remaining 30% of healthy controls plus MCI and patients with AD were used to assess the heterogeneity...”

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: There is no report of applying the trained reference normative model to an independent external healthy dataset solely for validation. The external application involved recalibration/transfer learning using ADNI controls, followed by analysis of clinical heterogeneity, not validation of model fit in an independent healthy cohort.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “Next, these estimates were conditioned to our specific context, using an adapted transfer learning approach... recalibrated to the ADNI data set using 70% of healthy controls per ADNI site...”

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: hierarchical Bayesian regression with age and sex covariates, pooling across sites via shared priors; transfer learning to adapt to ADNI; implementation specified with software and version (PCNtoolkit v0.20).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text:
“A hierarchical Bayesian regression model was trained on multisite data to generate normative models per region using the covariates age and sex... adaptively pools parameter estimates across sites via a shared prior...”
“Next, these estimates were conditioned... using an adapted transfer learning approach...”
“All modeling steps are performed using PCNtoolkit (version 0.20).”

Final sample sizes are reported at multiple points (total scanned n=1,492 across 62 sites; final n=1,027 after reserving 70% of controls for calibration).
